Help page fm1Mult; Grp is the Block-within-Location whole-plot id, already a column. Location is an ordered covariate. obs is a row id (ignored); Fe and Block are unused but usable columns. Littell Data Set 2.8.1.
Help page fm1PBIB (output 1.7 pp.24-25). Block is an ordered factor but a grouping id. Partially balanced incomplete block experiment, Littell Data Set 1.5.1.

Help page fm1SIMS (output 7.4 p.262), random-coefficient regression of test gain on pre-test with class-specific intercept and slope. Class is an ordered factor but a grouping id. Littell section 7.2.2 (Second International Mathematics Study).
Help page fm1Semi, a split-plot; Grp is the ET-by-Wafer whole-plot id, already a column and an ordered factor used as a grouping id. Wafer is a component of Grp, unused. Littell Data Set 2.2(b).

Help page gives no model (only str). Rendered from the nested design at low: uTeacher (the Method/Teacher unique code) random, pupils within teacher, teaching method and teacher experience as covariates. Student is a within-cell replicate index (ignored); Teacher is the within-method teacher index, unused. uTeacher is an ordered factor but a grouping id. Littell Data Set 5.6.

Help page gives no model (only str). Rendered from the nested design at low: uTeacher (the Method/Teacher unique code) random, pupils within teacher, IQ a pupil covariate. Teacher is the within-method index, unused. uTeacher is an ordered factor but a grouping id. Littell Data Set 5.7.

Help page gives no model (only str). Model recalled from Littell section 7.2: random-coefficient regression of yield on soil moisture with variety-specific intercept and slope (parallel to SIMS, section 7.2.2). Variety is an ordered factor but a grouping id.

Help page gives no model (only str) and names two numeric responses (delta, Thick); took Thick (thickness) as the response and ignored delta as the alternate. uWafer is the unique group/temperature/type/wafer id (grouping); Site is the within-wafer replicate and Wafer a component of uWafer, both ignored. Temperature is an ordered covariate; Group, Temperature and Type are between-wafer factors. Littell Data Set 5.8. RULE GAP: two candidate responses, no documented model.

Help page fm1Weight (output 3.1 p.91). Subj is the Program/Subject unique id (grouping); Subject is the within-program subject index, ignored. Subj is an ordered factor but a grouping id. Weight-lifting strength over time, Littell Data Set 3.2(a).

formula: mathgain ~ mathkind + sex + minority + ses + housepov + yearstea + mathknow + mathprep + (1 | schoolid) + (1 | classid)
notes: Help page describes the Study of Instructional Improvement (outcome mathgain) but gives no formula. Three-level model (pupils in classes in schools), classid nested in schoolid, recalled from West, Welch & Galecki (2007) and Galecki & Burzykowski (2013), with pupil-, class- and school-level covariates. childid is the pupil id (ignored). mathknow has missing values.

formula: visual ~ visual0 + time + treat.f + time:treat.f + (1 | subject)
notes: Help page describes the ARMD trial (longitudinal visual acuity, 4-52 weeks) but gives no formula. Linear mixed model recalled from Galecki & Burzykowski (2013): baseline visual0, time, treatment and the time-by-treatment interaction, random subject intercept. time.f and tp are alternate time codings and miss.pat the missingness pattern, all ignored.

Help page states the grouping factors (pupil id and attainment target) are crossed; no formula given. Crossed random-effects model recalled from Galecki & Burzykowski (2013). scorec is the number of items correct per target (0-9), an integer count; the item count is embedded in the target label, not a column, so no trials column is named.

formula: spec.fo ~ prt.f + age.f + sex.f + occ.f + fiber.f + bmi + (1 | id)
notes: Help page describes the Progressive Resistance Training trial (muscle fibers within subjects) but gives no formula; prt is the fiber-level table merged with subject covariates. Model recalled from Galecki & Burzykowski (2013) with specific force spec.fo as the response and a random subject intercept; the book also explores occasion-by-fiber and training interactions. iso.fo is the alternate (isometric) force response, ignored.

Help page describes a longitudinal RCT of methylprednisolone for severe alcoholic hepatitis (serum bilirubin weekly, weeks 0-4) but gives no formula. Rendered from the design at low: treatment-by-time growth with random subject intercept and slope. baseline is the week-0 sbvalue copied onto every row (alternate/derived response), ignored to avoid collinearity. Source Vonesh & Chinchilli (1997).

formula: vsae ~ age2 * sicdegp + I(age2^2) * sicdegp + (age2 + I(age2^2) | childid)
notes: Help page describes a longitudinal autism study (Vineland socialization vsae by age) but gives no formula. Quadratic growth model by SICD group recalled from West, Welch & Galecki (the kwelch source): vsae on age2 (and age2 squared) interacted with sicdegp, random child growth curve. sicdegp is labelled a plain factor (low/med/high), not an ordered factor, so no type declared. gender, race and bestest2 are unused but usable columns.

Canonical Gelman & Hill (2007) varying-intercept radon model: floor indicator basement (within county) and county-level soil uranium, random county intercept. The response is already in log pCi/L (no raw radon column). county.name is the county label (alternate id), ignored. Published Stan/ARM example model.

Help page gives lmer(lnw ~ exper + (exper | id)) in a dontrun block. Singer & Willett (2003) ALDA wage-trajectory example; response is log wages. hgc.9 (centered hgc) and the ue.* columns are transforms of hgc and uerate (derived), ignored; ged, postexp, black, hispanic, hgc and uerate are unused but usable columns.

Help example m1 lmer(yield ~ -1 + trt + (1|rep/mp/sp)); mp=paste(row,spacing) and sp=paste(row,spacing,stock) are the main plots and subplots, so the grouping factors are rep and the composites row:spacing and row:spacing:stock (the merge builds them and the nesting). trt (factor) is the full treatment code 100*spacing+10*stock+gen; spacing and stock also enter the plot composites, gen and pos are unused columns. Cornelius and Archbold 1989 split-split-plot analysis.

Help page: Besag used the data to show spatial variation but did no analysis (examples only desplot); Kempton, Statistical Methods for Plant Variety Evaluation, pp.91-92, cited. RULE GAP: rendered from the design as a crossed row/col spatial random-effects model with the two check varieties (gen: Bounty, Huntsman) fixed; row and col treated as crossed grouping factors with replication.

Help page describes a multi-environment alpha-design trial (zones over locations over reps over incomplete alpha blocks over genotypes) but the examples only draw a bwplot. Buntaran 2020 (Crop Science) does a stagewise mixed-model analysis, not reproduced here. Rendered from the design at low: genotype fixed, environment hierarchy random (zone, loc, loc:rep, loc:rep:alpha; merge builds composites and nesting).

Help example m0 lmer(yield ~ gen + (1|rep/block)); matches Burgueno et al. 2000 ASREML guide p.26. block (12 levels) nested in rep (3 levels, 4 blocks each); row and col are spatial coordinates used only by the asreml spatial models m1-m13, left as unused columns.

Help example m2 asreml(yield ~ 1, random = ~ gen, resid = ~ ar1(xf):ar1(yf)) with xf/yf from col/row; matches Burgueno et al. 2000. 280 new genotypes are unreplicated with one check (G000) planted every 4th column, so gen is an almost-all-singleton grouping factor (only the check repeats) - an extreme imbalance case. row and col drive the spatial AR1 residual (not grouping); oddcol in m3 is built in the example, not a column.

Help example m0 asreml(yield ~ 1+env, random = ~ gen) - the base multi-environment model with genotype random and environment fixed; later models m1-m4 add a pedigree relationship matrix via vm(gen, ped.ainv), not a simple grouping. male and female are the diallel parents (components of the gen cross), left as unused columns. Butron et al. 2004.

Help example fits a fixed-effects lm(yield ~ 0 + gen + rep + cov) where cov is a derived average-neighbour covariate built in the example (not a column); Connolly et al. 1993. RULE GAP: no mixed model is documented; rendered from the four-rep single-drill RCB design with rep as a random block and variety (gen) fixed. matur (maturity group, constant within gen), row and col (spatial) left as unused columns.

Help example m2 lmer(yield ~ fert*soil*calcium + (1|rep) + (1|rep:fert) + (1|rep:soil) + (1|rep:fert:calcium)); the strip-split-plot of SAS/STAT guide example 23.5. The example drops the rep:soil:fert stratum for convergence (the afex block that adds it is inside if(0)).

Help example fits a fixed-effects anova lm(sqrt(white+.5) ~ rep + gen); Gomez and Gomez 1984 p.300, table 7.21. RULE GAP: no mixed model documented; rendered from the 14-variety, 3-rep RCB design with rep as a random block and gen fixed. white is percent white heads, modeled on the sqrt(white+.5) scale per Gomez; raw column white named as response.

Help example m1 aov(height ~ rep + manage + time + manage:time + Error(rep/manage/time)); Gomez and Gomez 1984 p.481, table 6.11. Translated to lmer: whole-plot management, sub-plot time, two subsamples per plot (the Within/residual stratum). sample (S1,S2) is the subsample index, left as an unused column.

Help example m0 aov(yield ~ nf*management*gen + Error(rep/nf/management)) with nf=factor(nitro); Gomez and Gomez 1984 p.143-153. Split-split-plot: nitrogen main plot, management sub-plot, variety sub-sub-plot; translated to lmer. nitro (5 doses) is used qualitatively as factor(nitro), so it is both a fixed factor and part of the whole-plot composite rep:nitro. col and row (field position) left as unused columns.

Help model m3l, the full-table lme (Schabenberger and Pierce 2002, p.518, proc mixed output 7.27): group-specific (age x species) quadratic trends in time with a random intercept and ti-slope per tree, plus a corExp(day|tree) residual correlation lme4 cannot express. ti=day/100 and ti2=ti^2 are built in the example from the day column. 40 trees (10 per species x age cell), repeated measures about every 5 days; the earlier models m1n/m1l/m2l fit the A2,S2 subgroup only and are not used (the survey uses the full table). Linear in parameters (polynomial in time), not nonlinear.

formula: adg ~ line + damage + line:damage + weanage + weight + (1|sire)
notes: Help example fits a fixed-effects lm(adg ~ 1 + line + sire + damage + line:damage + weanage + weight) with sire fixed; Harvey 1960 (an early least-squares-means paper). RULE GAP: rendered as the classic sire variance-component model with sire (9 sires, nested in the 3 dam lines) as a random grouping factor; the dmm package vignette (cited) gives a full mixed analysis. calf is the steer row id (ignored); weanage and weight are continuous covariates.

Aggregated ordinal frequency table (count = plants per plot in each disease category C1<C2<C3). Help examples only cross-tabulate and mosaic; the model is recalled from Jansen 1990 (Applied Statistics 39:75-84, Table 1), a threshold model for ordinal data with extravariation. The extravariation is a random plot effect; a plot is one population (male x female cross) in one block, so the grouping factor is the composite block:male:female (48 plots, 3 category rows each). count is the frequency weight (ignored).

Help example m1 clmm2(damage ~ rod + energy + gen + weight, weights=count, random=rod:energy, link=probit) and alternative m2 clmm(... + (1|rod:energy)); Keen and Engel 1997 (Statistica Neerlandica 51:129). Ordinal mixed model over an aggregated count table: damage D1<D2<D3<D4, count is the frequency weight (ignored). rod and energy are fixed and also form the random composite rod:energy; the weight column is the weight-class factor, not a model weight.

Help page gives no model (examples only desplot and group_by(gen) means); Kirk and Goulden 1925, a highly-replicated unrandomised variety trial with check plots every 5th row. RULE GAP: rendered from the variety-trial design with genotype (gen, varieties plus repeated checks) as a random grouping factor estimating variety means; the check varieties are far more replicated than the entries (imbalance). rep is labelled a replicate (not a block), row and col are spatial, left as unused columns.

Uniformity trial of barley; help examples fit an asreml model random=~x+y+ar1(x):ar1(y) with x=factor(col) and y=factor(row) (Piepho & Williams 2010). Random intercepts on row and col rendered in lme4; the separable AR1(col)xAR1(row) spatial term is not expressible and is dropped. Filed per the uniformity rule because the examples fit random terms on table columns (row, col).

Multi-environment tomato trial (Ortiz et al. 2007); help fits PLS of the GxE matrix on environmental covariates (sibling ortiz.tomato.covs), no mixed model. Crossed genotype and environment random intercepts rendered from the MET design; one yield per gen x env, some cells missing. weight is an alternate response, ignored.

Help fits a fixed betareg(y ~ gen + bunt + gen:bunt) on pct/100 and suggests bunt should be included as a random effect (Salmon 1938). Rendered with bunt random and genotype fixed; the strong gen:bunt interaction is noted but not carried. rep (2 levels) is the layout repeat, left as an unused column. pct is a percentage, so continuous.

Multi-environment rice trial (Seshu & Cady 1984); help fits a pooled lm(yield ~ rad + mint + I(mint^2)) with no grouping and calls the quadratic fit questionable. loc grouping inferred from locations repeated across years; country, year and month left as unused columns.

Split-plot repeated-measures asparagus (Snedecor & Cochran; O'Neill 2010). Help fits lmer(yield ~ trt + year + trt:year + (1|block) + (1|block:trt)) and an equivalent asreml split-plot; year is used as a factor. block:trt is the whole-plot composite built from its parts. An antedependence residual variant (m3) has the same random part, not a separate grouping.

Multi-environment potato trial (Tai 1971); yield is the mean of a 4-rep RCB at each environment, so cell means. Help gives only a dotplot and a stability-analysis stub, no mixed model. Crossed genotype and environment random intercepts rendered from the MET design. variety is the genotype name (duplicate of gen); loc and year are the components of env; all ignored.

Dose-response of herbicide on larkspur in 3 reps (Turner et al. 1992). Help fits a pooled glm(prop ~ rate, weights=live, binomial) with no random term; rep (3 blocks) rendered as a random intercept. rate is a continuous dose. Response is dead out of live (binomial).

Multi-environment wheat trial (Vargas et al. 1998); help fits PLS of the GxE matrix on environmental covariates (sibling vargas.wheat2.covs). Crossed genotype and environment random intercepts rendered from the 8-genotype by 21-environment design. RULE GAP: the stored yield is already environment- and genotype-centered (mean-zero GxE residuals, with negative values), so the main-effect variance components are near zero; the grouping dimensions are still real.

Lattice-square variety trial of 49 soybeans in 4 reps (Weiss & Cox 1939). Help fits a fixed lm/asreml yield ~ rep + rep:col + rep:row + gen (matching Weiss table 7). Mixed rendering treats rep and the incomplete row/column blocks within rep as random, genotype fixed; rep:col and rep:row are composites built from their parts.

Classic Rothamsted split-plot (Yates 1935). Help fits lmer(yield ~ factor(nitro) * gen + (1|block/gen)) (m3); block/gen gives block and block:gen (whole plots). grain is yield in pounds (yield = 4*grain) and straw an alternate response, both ignored; row and col are plot coordinates left as unused columns. RULE GAP: nitro is modelled as factor(nitro) but stored as float, so the merge's column rule will count it continuous rather than a 4-level factor, and types cannot fix it on an R file (ordered only).

Help model m4 adds a linear col trend to m3 (better AIC), so col becomes a covariate. Same block and block:gen grouping; grain and straw ignored as in model 1. Same nitro-as-float RULE GAP noted for model 1.

Multi-environment powdery-mildew scores of 24 wheat genotypes (Lillemo et al. 2011); help computes nonparametric stability statistics and a GGE biplot, no mixed model. Crossed genotype and environment random intercepts rendered from the MET design. RULE GAP: score is a mean across reps and each environment used one of four measurement scales (0-5, 1-9, 0-9, percent; the scale column), so the response is not on a common scale; the grouping dimensions are still real.

USDA state-level sorghum yields circa 1900-2011, one average yield per state per year. Help fits a fixed per-state piecewise lm of yield on year (for Illinois), no grouping. state grouping with year as a time covariate rendered from the panel; acres harvested left as an unused column. RULE GAP: the response is a state-year average (aggregate statistic), not an observation-level measurement; filed for its longitudinal grouping.
